newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Big out-of-money Bund puts traded, vol up.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Big out-of-money Bund puts traded, vol up.

text.p: Large trades in deep out-of-the-money Bund puts were the talking point in the European debt options market on Wednesday as dealers said one firm was scrambling to neutralise a money-losing strategy.

Implied volatility of Bund options firmed up ahead of U.S. inflation data and stayed at their higher levels following the release of the numbers, which showed a scant 0.1 percent increase in U.S. consumer prices during January.
A salesman at a European bank said the put trades seemed to be based on a position taken by a British house at the turn of the year which had gone "horribly wrong".
By 1410 GMT, dealers said around 9,000 lots of Bund puts with a 91.50 strike had traded.
"That's 10 points out of the money," said Luke White, broker at Fimat Futures UK, noting the rarity of such an out-of-the-money trade.
The European bank salesman said delta in those puts was down to zero, showing that moves in the underlying market were having next to no effect on the options premiums.
March Bund futures traded as low as 99.28 at the start of 1997, but they have risen more than four points since then and remain within a firm uptrend.

Elsewhere, trading activity was mixed and centred on the June contract, which becomes the front month, when March expires on Friday. The initial volume of trade was dampened by technical problems with screen prices, they said.
"There has been quite a lot of activity but it has all been quite a mixed bag really," said a French Broker on the LIFFE floor.
Brokers quoted implied volatility of options on the June Bund future at 5.6 to 5.7 percent, compared with 5.46 percent mid-vol late Tuesday.
For April implied vol levels were also higher around 5.55 to 5.7 percent and for May 5.5 to 5.65 percent. On Tuesday April vol was quoted at 5.43 percent and May at 5.44 percent.
White said paper sellers had been trying to sell vol in anticipation of a benign U.S. CPI figure.
The rise was smaller than the forecast 0.3 percent.
Brokers said June volatiltiy had been actively trading around 5.6 percent with locals buying and paper selling.
